You are a code-quality reviewer (EFFICIENCY angle only). Do NOT hunt for correctness bugs. Do NOT edit any files.

Repo: /home/nick/work/andesim — a C++20 CLI driver under `driver/`. Read the diff under review first: `/tmp/simplify_scope.diff`. It implements a CLI redesign with a data-driven `andesim --help` tree in `driver/main.cpp` and a `plan_step_rc_error` string builder in `driver/run_plan.cpp`.

Your job: flag wasted work the diff INTRODUCES — redundant computation, repeated I/O, work that could be done once, unnecessary allocations/copies in hot or repeated paths. This is a short-lived CLI process so micro-optimizations on one-shot help printing are NOT worth flagging; focus only on genuinely wasteful patterns.

Read `driver/main.cpp`, `driver/run_plan.cpp`, `driver/run_plan.hpp` for context.

Specifically consider:
- `plan_step_rc_error` builds a std::string via repeated `+` concatenation — is that on a hot/repeated path or a one-shot error path? (Only flag if genuinely hot.)
- The help render functions call `is_dev_mode()` (which may read an env var) once per option row in a loop — is that a repeated syscall/getenv that should be hoisted out of the loop? Check what `is_dev_mode()` does (driver/dev_mode.*).
- Any per-row work that could be hoisted.

For each finding return: `file:line` — one-line summary — the cheaper alternative and WHY it matters here (or note it's negligible). If nothing is worth changing, say "clean — one-shot CLI paths, no meaningful waste." Be honest about negligible-impact findings; do not invent work.

1	// The phase-plan executor (F6) -- the C++ analog of runner.run_session, minus
2	// the dropped QEMU2 handback. run_plan spawns each leg of a Plan in order,
3	// threads the drained hybrid_state_v1 file forward (leg N's --handoff-out is
4	// leg N+1's --resume-from-qemu), and reports each leg's mcycle/minstret.
5	//
6	// plan_argvs is the pure core (no spawn, no mmap): it resolves each Step's
7	// engine + role against the registry and fills the invoke template with the
8	// threaded state paths, so the argv construction is unit-testable in isolation.
9	#ifndef ANDESIM_RUN_PLAN_HPP
10	#define ANDESIM_RUN_PLAN_HPP
11	
12	#include <string>
13	#include <vector>
14	
15	#include "engine_descriptor.hpp"
16	#include "plan.hpp"
17	
18	namespace andes_sim {
19	
20	// The framework-owned values shared by every leg of a run: the resolved
21	// shared-mmap path/size/base and the QEMU plugin path. Per-leg values
22	// (bin/state_in/state_out) are derived by plan_argvs from this + the threading.
23	struct RuntimeCtx {
24	  std::string mmap_path;
25	  long long mem_size = 0;
26	  std::string mmap_base = "0x0";
27	  std::string plugin_path;
28	};
29	
30	// hw-config sync: the QEMU fast leg models the hardware the accurate-leg
31	// engine measures, so its -cpu vlen follows that engine's descriptor. 512 is
32	// the fallback for engines that report none. One definition, used by both the
33	// plan executor ({vlen} fill) and the hybrid banner.
34	inline long synced_vlen(long engine_vlen) {
35	  return engine_vlen > 0 ? engine_vlen : 512;
36	}
37	
38	// A trigger's per-leg argv contribution, dispatched by the leg's role. The
39	// QEMU plugin takes its trigger as a comma-suffix folded INTO the one `-plugin`
40	// token (so it rides the `{trigger}` placeholder); vsim takes separate tokens
41	// appended to its argv. marker contributes nothing (plugin/vsim detect the markers
42	// themselves).
43	struct LegTriggerArgs {
44	  std::string plugin_suffix;        // qemu fast-leg: appended to {trigger}
45	  std::vector<std::string> extra;   // vsim accurate-leg: appended tokens
46	};
47	
48	// Map `t` onto `role`'s argv contribution. marker -> empty. pc -> qemu
49	// `,enter_pc=<enter_pc>` / vsim `--hybrid-exit-pc <exit_pc>`. icount -> qemu
50	// `,icount=<qemu_icount>` / vsim `--hybrid-icount <vsim_icount>`. Roles other
51	// than fast-leg/accurate-leg get nothing. A missing required param or an
52	// unknown trigger kind sets `err` (and returns an empty contribution).
53	//
54	// NOTE (altitude debt): these flag spellings are framework-side per-engine
55	// knowledge -- the one place F9 hardcodes a fast/accurate engine's CLI, unlike
56	// the base argv which comes from each engine's `--describe` invoke template.
57	// This is a deliberate scope cut: the principled form (per-(trigger,role) argv
58	// templates carried in `--describe`, filled by build_argv like `invoke`) would
59	// extend the F2 engine contract and is left for a later feature.
60	LegTriggerArgs leg_trigger_args(const Trigger& t, const std::string& role,
61	                                std::string& err);
62	
63	// Build every step's concrete argv, threading state files under `workdir`:
64	//   state_in[0]  = ""                       (cold start; no resume)
65	//   state_in[i]  = state_out[i-1]           (prior leg's drain)
66	//   state_out[i] = workdir/"state-<i>.bin"  (this leg's drain)
67	// Each step's engine is looked up in `engines` by id and its `role` template is
68	// filled via build_argv. Pure (no spawn). Returns one argv per step; on any
69	// error (unknown engine/role, unresolved placeholder) returns {} and sets `err`.
70	std::vector<std::vector<std::string>> plan_argvs(
71	    const Plan& plan, const std::vector<EngineDescriptor>& engines,
72	    const std::string& workdir, const RuntimeCtx& ctx, std::string& err);
73	
74	struct PlanOptions {
75	  int timeout_ms = 90000;     // per-leg spawn timeout
76	  int expect_rc = 200;        // drain success code (kExitHandoffToQemu)
77	  std::string plugin_path;    // "" => $VSIM_PLUGIN else repo default
78	};
79	
80	// Compose the "plan step N exited wrong" diagnostic. A drain step (expect_rc is
81	// the handoff/drain code) that exits 0 ran the ELF to completion without ever
82	// reaching its ROI boundary -- the marker/pc trigger never fired; say so and
83	// name the trigger kind so the fix (right ELF / right --trigger) is obvious.
84	// Any other mismatch gets the plain "expected X, got Y" line.
85	std::string plan_step_rc_error(size_t step, const Step& s, int expect_rc,
86	                               int got_rc);
87	
88	// Execute `plan`: resolve the plugin, acquire the shared mmap (allocate one
89	// under /dev/shm when plan.mmap_path is empty, and own it), spawn each leg with
90	// a timeout, require exit == expect_rc, and read back each leg's mcycle/minstret
91	// from its drained state file. Returns the per-leg results; on the first failure
92	// `error` describes it and `phases` holds whatever completed before it.
93	PlanResult run_plan(const Plan& plan,
94	                    const std::vector<EngineDescriptor>& engines,
95	                    const PlanOptions& opts = {});
96	
97	}  // namespace andes_sim
98	
99	#endif  // ANDESIM_RUN_PLAN_HPP

I have all the context needed. Let me analyze the two flagged concerns and any per-row work.

**Verdict: clean — one-shot CLI paths, no meaningful waste.**

The diff introduces no wasteful work on any hot or repeated path. Addressing each concern explicitly:

`driver/run_plan.cpp:43-55` — `plan_step_rc_error` builds its string via repeated `+`. NOT hot. It is called from exactly one site (`run_plan.cpp:266`) inside the `if (r.rc != opts.expect_rc)` branch, which `break`s immediately after. So it runs at most once per `run_plan` call, only on the error path — and `run_plan` has just spawned simulator subprocesses each with a 90s timeout. One error-string build is invisible next to that. Negligible.

`driver/run_plan.cpp:49` — `PlanOptions{}.expect_rc` constructs a throwaway `PlanOptions` just to read the default `expect_rc` (200). Its `std::string` members are empty (SSO, no heap). Same one-shot error path. Negligible; not worth changing.

`driver/main.cpp:140` and `driver/main.cpp:148` — `is_dev_mode()` (which is `std::getenv("ANDESIM_DEV")`, per `driver/dev_mode.hpp:15-18`) is called per row inside the option/target loops. This is NOT a meaningful repeated syscall:
- `getenv` is a userspace scan of the `environ` array, not a syscall.
- Short-circuit `o.dev && !is_dev_mode()` means it only fires on dev rows — 4 of 14 in `kRunOpts`, 1 of 3 in `kListTargets`.
- `print_run_block`/`print_list_block` each run once per process (from `print_usage` or `print_subcommand_help`, both called once in `main`). This is one-shot help printing.

So at most ~4 userspace array scans across the whole process lifetime. Hoisting `is_dev_mode()` to a single local would be a correct readability tidy, but the efficiency impact is zero — exactly the one-shot help-printing micro-optimization the brief says not to flag.

No other per-row work to hoist: the help model is `constexpr` arrays of `const char*` literals (no allocations, no copies), rows are iterated by `const&`, and `print_opt` formats into a stack buffer (`char left[96]`, no heap). Nothing repeated, nothing copied unnecessarily.
